request:
fix: reject binary remote form with empty file-offset table as 400 Bad Request (#17576)

When a malformed binary remote-form payload has file_offsets_length === 0 but its devalue data references a File, file_offsets remains undefined. Consequently, devalue's File reviver attempted to read file_offsets[index], throwing an unhandled TypeError (Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')) which resulted in an internal server error (HTTP 500) rather than an invalid request response.

Guard file_offsets !== undefined during File metadata validation so malformed payloads referencing missing file offsets cleanly throw a deserialize_error and respond with HTTP 400 Bad Request.

Fixes #17576

Signed-off-by: praveen-kumary <praveenkumar2000y@gmail.com>

request:
breaking: don't abort navigation when calling `invalidate(All)` during navigation (#16188)

When a navigation starts, `invalidate(All)` will no longer abort that
navigation - previously it indirectly did that because both invalidation
and navigation shared the same navigation token; then navigation thought
"oh I'm outdated I abort".

Now there's a separate invalidation token so we can handle each case
sensibly:
- when invalidation finishes after goto finishes, it will not apply its
stale data. It _will_ apply redirects though since technically it's the
last navigation that happened and so it should take precedence
- when invalidation finishes before goto finishes, it will apply, but it
will not abort the navigation

Closes #9354

---------

request:
fix(static): respond with 404 when a public asset is missing on disk (#4588)

* fix(static): respond with 404 when a public asset is missing on disk

* refactor(static): detect missing assets in the asset reader

Translate ENOENT inside the generated node reader instead of the runtime
handler, so all three readers share one contract: resolving with no value
means the manifest entry has no data behind it.

This keeps Node errno checks out of `src/runtime`, restores the handler to
a synchronous fallthrough for non-asset requests, and covers the `inline`
reader, which already returned no data for a missing payload and until now
served it as an empty 200.

* refactor(static): drop the warning for a pruned public asset

Both reported cases (nuxt#29078, nuxt#33033) prune the public dir on
purpose - uploading it to a CDN, or stripping sourcemaps after sending
them to Sentry - so the missing file is a standing configuration rather
than a one-off fault, and warning per read only spams the log.

request:
fix(ecosystem-qa): drop the Playwright cache mount that the native sandboxes never read

bwrap and seatbelt give the agent a private home and mount a path only at its host path, and Playwright looks for browsers under the home it is given, so the mounted cache was never found. Pointing `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` at it instead would make every `playwright install` in the sandbox wait on a lock it cannot create in a read-only directory, so the agent keeps installing a missing browser into its own home, as the prompt tells it to.

request:
fix(ecosystem-qa): make the native sandboxes usable for a local run

The yarn 1 shim reads the real home's .yarnrc and every rc file above the worktree, so those
files are mounted read-only one by one; a read-only mount of the clone would deny writes in the
worktree. The clone moves out of the monorepo tree so no monorepo rc file sits above it.
Claude Code writes to /tmp/claude-<uid> whatever TMPDIR says, so it gets CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR on
a mounted directory. The install wrapper keeps the install output as install.log in the evidence,
because the setup hook only reported the exit code.
